- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in early days of the 30-day horizon.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing near-term price spikes.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.80, 80.24), model overreacts with overshoots in the immediate forecast window.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to pull prices back toward historical averages after peaks.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the final 5–10 days, underestimating the true price decline or stabilization.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias, especially when true prices are above 70 — likely due to insufficient volatility modeling.
- Forecasts are more accurate when true prices are near the 70–75 range, but fail when prices are above 80 or below 65.
